fact: Donald Trump's 1987 book 'The Art of the Deal' reached number one on The New York Times Best Seller list, staying there for 13 weeks and remaining on the list for a total of 48 weeks.
The book coined the term 'truthful hyperbole,' described as 'an innocent form of exaggeration—and... a very effective form of promotion.' Trump reportedly loved this phrase.
In 1988, plans were announced for a television film based on 'The Art of the Deal,' but by 1991, these plans had been largely abandoned.
The book has been translated into over a dozen languages, expanding its reach globally.
Trump has cited 'The Art of the Deal' as one of his proudest accomplishments and his second-favorite book after the Bible.
The book's success contributed significantly to Trump's image as a savvy businessman and dealmaker, influencing his public persona and future ventures.
The book has sold somewhere between hundreds of thousands and millions of copies since its first publication in 1987.
Trump's self-promotion, best-selling book, and media celebrity status led one commentator in 2006 to call him 'a poster-child for the 'greed is good' 1980s.'
The book has been credited with inspiring Mark Burnett to create 'The Apprentice,' the reality TV show that further elevated Trump's fame.
